### 4.1 Mod project model + revisions (size L)
Typed project: `ModSpec`/content IR (items, mobs, abilities, GUIs, quests, recipes, loot, biomes...), code files, assets, datapacks, config, dependencies, tests, requirement IDs. Stored as immutable revisions with diffs; each revision traces to exact inputs and toolchain; the last passing revision is always preserved. `schemaVersion` with explicit migrations; JSON Schema as the portable contract, Zod types in code. New tables (project, revision, asset, namespace) need an owner-approved DB migration deploy. Chat history is not the project.

### 4.2 Registries and reserved namespaces (S-M)
### 4.10 Per-game adapter contract (S, define in R0)
Artifact types and routes; toolchain profile and deny-list scan; version registry; knowledge pack; asset formats and **delivery** (Minecraft: server-pushed pack; Valheim: client zip; Terraria/Palworld: none; tModLoader: client mod); install rules; test lane; maturity level. Add `game` to every id and registry. Texture/Sound studios light up only where the adapter declares an asset format and delivery path. A realistic 3D/PBR profile is a later track; build only the interfaces now.

### 4.11 Data packs (M)
Typed spec -> per-version emitters (the AI never hand-writes JSON); schema source vanilla-mcdoc (MIT); static validation then boot a real headless Paper and test over RCON. MVP: recipes, loot, advancements, tags, functions, enchantments. Worldgen (biomes, structures, dimensions) later; `/reload` does not reload worldgen, so those changes need a restart.

## 5. Roadmap (ordered by dependency)
Calendar note: the review estimated R0-R2 at about 5-7 weeks including owner waits (UNVERIFIED judgement). The owner has beaten estimates; treat these as sequencing and relative size, not promises. (T) = real Minecraft client needed, (O) = owner action.

### R0 Foundation (about 4 working days)
| Day | Deliver | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Launch gates (verify hardened scan live (O), per-build engine-release record, paired flag guard, free-build abuse limit, per-build cost cap). Version registry with exact pack formats; fix `packFormatFor`; reproducible jars; JDK 25 beside 21 on node-2; classpath files by checksum; pin exact stable 26.x; nightly Fill check creates a "preview" row | Can prove what built every mod; 26.x compiles on node-2; pack numbers verified |
| 2 | Project model + revision store (DB migration (O)), ModSpec/IR, identifier registry + reserved namespaces, GameAdapter interface, minimal capability router, server-side tier gate (fail closed) | Spec stored per project; router explains limits; gate matrix test (4 plans x create/edit/keep/install) passes |
| 3 | ManagedPlugin mechanism, pack hosting (object storage + domain (O)), Pack Loader, **Test Flight lite** | A pack reaches a test server through the Pack Loader; boot gate runs on every build |
| 4 | Server inventory (read-only); eval harness extended (100+ prompts, per-version matrix, asset prompts) | Inventory report on a real server; baseline pass rate recorded per version |

### R1 Assets (about 5 days)
| Day | Deliver | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Texture slice: spec -> renderer -> validated pack; Style DNA; library of vanilla-style presets + uploads; hybrid JAR + pack install/uninstall (T) | Custom item shows its texture in a real client |
| 6 | Sound slice: tag library, synth presets, server-side mono Ogg, `sounds.json`, subtitles, multi-event per item/mob (T) | Right sounds play per event in a real client; Katara/free correctly blocked |
| 7 | Static 3D item models (the Glock) with display transforms, sounds, particles; vanilla-mob reskin + full sound set (banshee on 1.21.x) (T) | Glock and a banshee skin + sounds install and play |
| 8 | Studios v1: open a mod's assets, edit, re-push pack, revisions, library browsing, quality rubric + gallery (T) | Customer edits a texture/sound and sees it on the server; owner approves the gallery |
| 9 | Hardening: access test matrix, cost estimates per asset op, asset cost caps (2 critique rounds), caching by spec hash | Asset ops priced by measured work; no free bypass |

### R1b Full Texture and Sound Studios (owner priority, added 2026-10-10; Opus for the editor cores)
Moved forward from R3: the studios are a top priority, so the full editors come right after the first asset slice and before composition.
- **Texture Studio (top plan):** full pixel editor (layers, undo/redo, palettes and ramps, selection, tiling and 3D item preview, onion-skin for animated textures), library browsing and search, Style DNA applied across a whole mod, AI edits as non-destructive candidates with before/after diffs, reference-image-to-spec through a vision model, asset history, the quality rubric as a real review screen.
- **Sound Studio (Saka and up):** full waveform editor (zoom, regions, trim, fade, gain, pitch/time, layering, spectrum, loudness and true-peak readouts), library browsing and search by tag, synthesis presets, per-event mob/item sound sets, subtitle keys, non-destructive edit recipes, server-side Ogg export, asset history with waveform diffs.
- **Both:** shared studio core with per-game profiles (Minecraft pixel profile first); plan-tier gates enforced server-side; library follows the studio gate.
- **Done when:** a customer builds a complete set (e.g. banshee skin plus attack/hurt/death sounds) entirely in the studios without touching a prompt, and a real client shows and plays it (T).
- R3 keeps only animated creatures, gameplay designers and playtest scripts.

### Item model states and display contexts (owner question, 2026-10-10; queued after Studio UI part 1)
Today the pack builder emits ONE flat model per texture (handheld parent): one look, no states. Owner needs: how an item looks dropped, in an inventory slot, in first-person and third-person hand, on the head, in an item frame; and stateful items (a bow idle vs pulled back; a gun aiming/reloading).
- **ItemModelSpec v1** (new, in the asset spec): per-context display transforms (gui, ground, fixed/item frame, first/third person right+left hand, head) with per-category defaults (sword, tool, bow, gun, wand, shield) the owner/studio can override; named STATES each with a model/texture and the condition that selects it.
- **Mechanism (1.21.4+ item model definitions; names UNVERIFIED, must be checked against the docs and real servers before building):** `condition` on using_item, `range_dispatch` on use_duration/pull for pull stages, `select` on display_context, and plugin-set custom_model_data flags/strings (e.g. reloading, aiming); a custom bow is built on real bow behaviour with our item_model; a custom gun uses a consumable-style 'using' state for aiming and plugin flags for reload/cooldown. Limits: no free-form animation (texture frame animation via .mcmeta and fast model switching only; no real recoil). 1.21.1 needs the legacy predicate/custom-model-data overrides path (later).
- **Generator:** emits items/<name>.json (definition with conditions/range/select), one model JSON per state with its display block, and tests with golden hashes; the build prompt tells the plugin which states exist and the flag keys; registry capability checked per version.
- **Studio:** context switcher (hotbar, dropped, first-person, third-person, item frame, head) and a STATE scrubber (idle, pull 1-3, aim, reload) in the preview; correct 'in hand' placement (the grip in the hand: the first fix already requested of the Studio UI agent).
- **Later:** true 3D cuboid item models (the model pipeline) for guns/bows that should not be extruded sprites.

### Asset Library (owner requirement, 2026-10-10): one proper, cataloged, searchable library for sounds AND textures
The owner wants every asset cataloged and organized, not just filename-tagged. Shared design for both libraries:
- **Taxonomy as data** (committed JSON, not code): primary category, multi-valued **use cases** (where a mod uses it), free tags, descriptors derived from measured data (sound: duration class, intensity, pitch band, loopable heuristic, channels; texture: size, palette ramp, transparency, tileable, style), synonym table, and a licence/provenance ledger per asset (never asserting originality that has not been documented).
- **Sound categories:** Weapons (gunshot, reload, cocking, ricochet, melee swing, clash, bow), Creatures & Voices, Impacts & Destruction, Movement, Environment & Ambience, Doors & Mechanisms, UI & Alerts, Crowd & Reactions. **Use cases:** weapon_fire, weapon_reload, weapon_impact, melee, mob_ambient/hurt/death/attack/step, ability_cast, magic, boss_event, ui_notification, pickup_reward, block_interaction, door_mechanism, ambience_world, weather, explosion (gunshot + reload are both also tagged `weapon`).
- **Texture categories:** Items (weapon, tool, armor, food, potion, misc), Blocks (stone, wood, ore, plant, glass, decorative), Entity skins (humanoid, quadruped, flyer, ghost), GUI (button, panel, icon, HUD piece), Particles, and **Style DNA presets** (palette ramps, outline rule, noise level); sources: Cyrus-authored original template specs, the customer's uploads, textures from the customer's own projects, later community-shared; every texture carries provenance + licence status and passes the quality bar.
- **Search (both):** free text with synonym expansion and ranking (exact tag > category > name words), facets/filters, pagination, "similar to"; Postgres full-text first, embeddings only later; library browsing follows the studio plan gate (sound = Saka and up, texture = top plan).
- **Builds now (R1, by the sound agent):** the sound library manifest + taxonomy + search API + a human catalog report for the owner to review. **Next:** the texture library (starter template specs authored as DSL, quality-checked) and a **unified catalog layer** (`lib/cyrus/library`) that serves sounds, textures and later models through one interface, with customer uploads stored as Cyrus-prefixed records; then the browse/search UI inside the studios (design mockups in progress).




### Motion, Animation and Effects: FOUNDATION (owner decision, 2026-10-10)
Owner: motion/animation/effects is foundational and NOT Minecraft-only: AI (or a human) creates the motion a mod needs (banshee walk cycle, gun cock/fire/reload, car driving with doors opening and a character getting in, explosions, fire, water), with LIVE playable simulation in the studio, tied to the Texture and Sound studios; per-game specifics are handled in adapters when each game is added, but the foundation exists now.
State today: pieces only. Have: `spawn_particles` in the designer (budgeted), creature clips (BetterModel), item model states (bow pull, gun aim/reload), Model Studio layer 2 pose/animation timeline (in build; told to keep it game-neutral and extensible), sound library, catalog. Missing: the game-neutral Motion core.
- **Motion core (proposal):** tracks with typed kinds (transform, particle, sound-cue, light/material, event/state-machine), clips, triggers from the ability graph (`play_effect`), deterministic sampler, playback clock API (viewport exposes it), simulator contract, per-game exporter/adapter contract, presets in the catalog as kind `effect`/`motion`, caps (entities, particles, duration).
- **First slice that proves it end to end:** gun fire/reload state machine + a door hinge in Minecraft display entities, with sound cues from the library and a muzzle-flash particle preset.
- **Steps:** (1) Sonnet research R-motion-effects.md (running), (2) Opus architecture + design + mockups, (3) build core + Minecraft exporter + studio timeline/preview, (4) vehicle rig + character attach: NOT a Minecraft target (owner clarified 2026-10-10); the neutral core must be able to express it, the build waits for the first vehicle-capable game (FiveM/RedM etc.), (5) other games per adapter.

### Config and Stats Studio: FOUNDATION (owner request, 2026-10-10)
Owner: manual configuration/stat editors for every kind of mod (mob speed/health/attack damage and speed, weapon fire rate/reload/ammo, ability cooldowns, shop prices, boss phases...), so nobody must prompt the AI to change a number; Cyrus must know which tunables to OFFER per mod category; stats with a visual (walk speed, attack speed, scale) reflect live in the viewport/motion simulation. Game-neutral schema, per-game exporters.
State today: only the designers have it (every number becomes a config.yml setting; `edit without regenerating`; /<plugin> params|reload; `planDesignEdit` exposed but NOT wired); plain AI plugins are only told to 'put tunable values in config.yml'; imported mods have their own config.yml; no studio form editor; no category-aware tunable templates.
Plan: ConfigSpec (typed params, units, safe ranges, applies live/reload/restart, visual links), category templates (mob, melee, gun, armor, ability, boss, shop, quest, minigame, world, item, utility), the AI declares tunables and the build verifies they are read, values-only revisions delivered through the delivery orchestrator (no model, no build), schema inference for imported mods, presets, Config page in the studio shell. Agent launched (Opus, branch feature/cyrus-r23-config). Owner decision: ungated (editing numbers is not asset creation), recommended.

### R2 Composition, data packs, import (about 7 days)
| Day | Deliver | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| 10-11 | Static conflict engine on the inventory; severity report; reserved-namespace behaviour; mutation corpus (take a good mod, collide IDs) | Seeded conflicts caught with the right class and severity |
| 12 | Mod Pack Builder: manifest, merge (Weld/Beet evaluation), combined boot + differential boots, install/rollback as one unit | Two conflicting mods are caught, resolved or blocked; pack installs and rolls back as a unit |
| 13-14 | Datapack MVP: typed emitters per version, mcdoc validation, boot + RCON check | Valid datapack loads on every listed version |
| 15-16 | Import (source-only): ingestion limits, allowlist, attestation, strict vs attested scan, revision 0, change planner | An uploaded simple plugin source is edited by prompt, rebuilt, scanned, tested, installed; history kept |
| 16 | Public pass-rate page + evidence badges (boot-tested on exact version, scan hash, SBOM) | Numbers come from real runs |

### R3 Creatures, full studios, designers (L; after R2 is stable)
- **26.x creature pipeline**: BetterModel managed plugin; RigSpec compiler; 3 archetypes; 5 clips; banshee end to end; hitboxes and attacks; performance budget per server (T).
- **Full Texture and Sound Studios**: layers/undo/palettes/selection/tiling preview/onion skin; waveform, spectrum, layering; reference-image-to-spec via a vision model; asset history with diffs.
- **Gameplay Designers**, one at a time: Custom Item Designer; ability/event graph (typed triggers -> conditions -> actions compiled to validated code, no arbitrary scripts) with a verified component library; then GUI, quests/NPCs, bosses, progression, minigames. Auto-generated Dialog config screens (1.21.7+).
- **Playtest scripts** from spec acceptance criteria (Mineflayer).

### R4 World and reach (L)
Biomes, structures, dimensions (restart rule); glyph HUDs with honest limits (avoid core shaders); "Try it" throwaway server link; multi-version build from one ModSpec; legacy `custom_model_data` emitter for 1.21.1; Server Doctor for servers with no Cyrus mods; mod health telemetry (opt-in).

### R5 Beyond Minecraft Java (own programmes)
Fabric client-mod pipeline (narrow); the other five games as adapters (multi-game prompt, per-game maturity ladder); realistic 3D/PBR asset profile; Bedrock conversion. Each starts only when the previous layers are stable.

## 6. Cross-cutting
- **Testing/eval**: extend the existing harness (28 prompts, 28/28 built, 13/13 loaded on v6) to 100+ prompts per version; golden pack snapshots (canonical JSON + sorted file list + sha1); property tests for merge laws (idempotent, order-stable, no key loss); javap-verified API sheets in CI; contract test of the version registry; mutation corpus for conflicts. Per-version pass rates published only when measured.
- **Quality bar**: Style DNA, rubric metrics, vision-judge calibration, owner gallery sign-off.
- **Pricing**: show an estimate before building; price assets by measured work; no charge if validation fails before delivery; per-feature reserve rows (reconcile `katara/saka/yakko` vs `katara/saka/all` naming); free tier gets no assets and per-device/IP caps.
- **Operations**: treat prompt + sheets + rules + scanner + image as one engine release with canary and auto-rollback on eval regression; per-feature kill switches (asset generation, import, packs); node-2 capacity budget for test servers; prompt-injection hygiene (imported text only as quoted data, no network for the model, path allow-list on diffs).
- **Security**: scanner remains a policy check, not proof; fail closed; import profiles warn honestly; supply-chain pinning (sha256, image digests, lockfiles).
- **Telemetry funnel**: prompt -> spec -> build -> pass -> install -> pack accepted -> player joined -> day-7 retention; gate impressions and upgrade conversion.

| Import hardness (dependencies, scanner bans reflection/network that legitimate plugins use) | Allowlist + attested profile; source-only first |
| Scanner false sense of safety | Honest labels; no "safe" claim for imports |
| Cost blowout from asset critique loops | Cap rounds, cache by spec hash, per-build cost cap |
| Public pass-rate claims | Publish only measured numbers per version |
| Build service auth (subscription login) | API key + re-measured pricing before ANY public launch |

VM 88001 update and image rebuild (JDK 25 beside 21) and the hardened scan check; DB migration deploy approval (project/revision tables); object storage + domain for packs; a standing person with Minecraft for (T) days (and later Fabric); confirm or change the defaults in Section 2; weekly-usage allowance for the build weeks; API-key switch before public launch.

# AJ - Cyrus customer app + landing motion fix (r39, 2026-10-11)
Branch `feature/cyrus-r39-customer-app` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r39`), latest r2 `ce7d3cb83a` (r37, r38 grants, r40 notifications) merged in. NOT merged into r2, NOT deployed, no migration run, `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP` off.

## (0) Landing (not in git; left in `cyrus-designs/v7-landing/` for the parent to publish)
- Motion & effects card: 8 real-time three.js scenes on ONE shared WebGL renderer blitted into per-tile 2D canvases (`assets/js/motion.js`). Fire (meshgen AK: burst recoil, muzzle star + side flash, flash light, sparks, smoke, brass casings), Reload (meshgen drum LMG), Door (library `door-heavy-iron` glb + its Open/Slam_Shut clips, re-skinned planks/iron, light through the doorway, dust), Explosion, Flame, Smoke, Water (ripple shader), Arcane. 256 px procedural flipbooks with frame blending and correct additive/alpha. Reduced motion = one hero frame each; offscreen/paused tiles cost nothing; posters for no-WebGL.
- 3D card: PMREM studio environment, physical materials, soft shadows, auto-framing, slower rotate (`studio-env.js`).
- Playwright on node-2 at 1440 / reduced motion / 390: no console errors, no overflow; shots in `v7-landing/shots/`.

## (1)-(5) App (commits 1f8f16d078, 09a96a862e, a99106a512, b7f1c3c702, 9924afca54, fixes 3fe465c4e8, docs 7f6f67f171, merge 3cd0c6cb6c)
Shell, dashboard, projects + project page, new-mod flow, account. Details in docs "Cyrus customer app". Gate fails closed (switch + studio gate + preview gate on every page and action); Cyrus tables only via `cyrusDb`. Grants use r38's store (adapter in the app layer); notification prefs use r40's format and table.

## Ran
- `tsc` clean; full Cyrus suite **2577/2578**: the 1 failure is r40's `app/dashboard/cyrus/notifications/page.tsx` already on r2 (gate-pattern test), not this branch's code. Host-seam and data-split ratchets pass. New `test/cyrus-customer-app.test.ts` 14/14.
- Playwright on node-2 against `devhost dev` with fixtures (`scripts/cyrus/app-fixtures.ts`, `app-shots.mjs`): 20 shots `impl-shots/app-*.png` (dark, light, phone, tour, outsider 404). Fixed what they showed: link colours lost to CSS specificity, cost panel on the wrong side, phone tab bar and tour offset by the portal's transformed frame, long Test Flight pills.
- Real round trips in dev: API key create (shown once) and list, prefs save, data export request, grants state with `CYRUS_SERVER_GRANTS=1`.

## Not run
- `next build`, cyrus.my host mode in a browser (routing only unit-tested), a real install or rollback click (the APIs are the existing ones), real Stripe, notices actually sent.
- Personal API keys are not accepted by `/api/cyrus/v1` yet. Data requests are recorded only; staff handle them by hand.

const support: GameSupport = {
  id: "terraria",
  name: "Terraria",
  builds:
    "Server plugins (TShock) that run on your Nxeon Terraria server with no installs for players, and content mods (tModLoader) that add new weapons, enemies, bosses, biomes, music and visuals.",
  language: "C#",
  loader: {
    name: "TShock (server plugins) and tModLoader (content mods)",
    homepage: "https://github.com/Pryaxis/TShock",
    installDocs: "https://github.com/tModLoader/tModLoader/wiki/tModLoader-guide-for-players",
    licenseNote:
      "TShock and its NuGet package are GPL-3.0; tModLoader is MIT. The Terraria game itself is proprietary: Cyrus never ships game files or game art, generated mods only point at art the player's own installed game already has.",
  },
  versions: [...tshockRows, ...tmlRows],
  install: {
    // The default build (TShock plugin) is server-only; tModLoader mods are "both" and say so in clientNote.
    side: "server",
    serverPath: "/opt/terraria-plugins (TShock plugin .dll). tModLoader mods go in tModLoader/Mods with an enabled.json entry.",
    clientNote:
      "Server plugins: players install nothing and join with the normal game. Content mods: every player needs tModLoader (a free app on Steam for anyone who owns Terraria). When they join, the server sends them the mod automatically, and tModLoader shows a warning that the mod is not from the Steam Workshop; they accept it and the game reloads.",
    needsRestart: true,
    hotReload: false,
    packaging: "dll",
    reason:
      "Most requests become a server plugin: it runs on the server only, so it works with the normal game and nobody has to install anything. New items, enemies, bosses, biomes and visuals need a content mod instead, which every player must also run.",
  },
  verification: {
    method: "compile",
    notes:
      "Every generated mod first passes Cyrus's static checks (lib/cyrus/games/terraria.validate.ts). On the build host, a TShock plugin compiles with the .NET 9 SDK against the public TShock NuGet package, and a tModLoader mod compiles with the .NET 8 toolchain against the public tModLoader release, which builds the real .tmod file. Neither needs any game file. Not done yet: a live load-test on a throwaway server and an automatic build step in the Cyrus pipeline (see READINESS.md).",
    canRunSandbox: false,
  },
  dangerousApis: [
    { pattern: String.raw`\bSystem\.Diagnostics\.Process\b|\bProcess\.Start\s*\(|\bProcessStartInfo\b`, severity: "block", why: "Starting other programs is never allowed in a game mod (tModLoader rule 2) and is the classic way server plugins get abused." },
    { pattern: String.raw`\bDllImport\b|\bLibraryImport\b|\bNativeLibrary\.|\bMarshal\.(GetDelegateForFunctionPointer|AllocHGlobal|Copy)\b|\bunsafe\b|\bfixed\s*\(`, severity: "block", why: "Native code and raw pointers can crash the game or hide behaviour (tModLoader rule 3: no native libraries)." },
    { pattern: String.raw`\bAssembly\.(Load|LoadFrom|LoadFile|UnsafeLoadFrom)\s*\(|\bAppDomain\b|\bAssemblyLoadContext\b|\bActivator\.CreateInstance\s*\(\s*Type\.GetType`, severity: "block", why: "Loading code at run time means the mod can run code nobody reviewed." },
    { pattern: String.raw`\bCSharpCompilation\b|\bCSharpScript\b|\bMicrosoft\.CodeAnalysis\b|\bSystem\.Reflection\.Emit\b|\bDynamicMethod\b|\bILGenerator\b`, severity: "block", why: "Compiling or emitting code at run time hides what the mod really does." },
    { pattern: String.raw`\bSystem\.Net\.(Http|Sockets|WebClient|WebRequest|HttpListener)\b|\bHttpClient\b|\bWebClient\b|\bTcpClient\b|\bUdpClient\b|\bTcpListener\b|\bnew\s+Socket\s*\(|\bClientWebSocket\b|\bDns\.`, severity: "block", why: "Mods must not reach the internet or open their own connections: the game already syncs what it needs (tModLoader rule 2)." },
    { pattern: String.raw`\bRegistry\b|\bMicrosoft\.Win32\b|\bEnvironment\.(SetEnvironmentVariable|Exit|FailFast)\b|\bEnvironment\.GetFolderPath\b`, severity: "block", why: "Touching the operating system (registry, environment, killing the process) is outside what a game mod may do." },
    { pattern: String.raw`\bSteamworks\b|\bSteamUser\b|\bSteamFriends\b|\bSteamUGC\b|\bSteamAPI\b`, severity: "block", why: "Mods must not act on the player's Steam account (tModLoader rule 4)." },
    { pattern: String.raw`\bBinaryFormatter\b|\bSoapFormatter\b|\bNetDataContractSerializer\b|\bTypeNameHandling\.(All|Auto|Objects)\b`, severity: "block", why: "These serializers can run attacker-chosen code when they read a file or packet." },
    { pattern: String.raw`\bFile\.(Delete|Move|Replace|Copy|Encrypt)\s*\(|\bDirectory\.(Delete|Move)\s*\(|\bFileSystemInfo\.Delete\b|\.Delete\s*\(\s*(true|recursive)`, severity: "block", why: "Deleting or moving files can destroy worlds and characters (tModLoader rule 1). Mods only write their own config." },
    { pattern: String.raw`\bWorldFile\.|\bPlayer\.SavePlayer\b|\bMain\.(WorldPath|PlayerPath)\b|\bWorldGen\.(clearWorld|SaveAndQuit)\b|\bMain\.ActiveWorldFileData\b`, severity: "block", why: "Rewriting or wiping world/character saves is how mods silently ruin a game." },
    { pattern: String.raw`\bTShock\.(DB|UserAccounts|Groups|CharacterDB|Bans)\b|\bTShock\.Config\.Settings\b|\.(Group|Account)\s*=|\bUserAccountManager\b|\bGroupManager\b|\bTSPlayer\.Server\.SetTime|\bConsole\.ReadLine\b`, severity: "block", why: "A plugin must not change accounts, groups, bans or TShock's own settings. Generated plugins only add their own commands and permissions." },
    { pattern: String.raw`\bThread\.Sleep\s*\(|\bwhile\s*\(\s*true\s*\)|\bfor\s*\(\s*;\s*;\s*\)`, severity: "block", why: "Blocking or endless loops freeze the server's game loop for every player." },
    { pattern: String.raw`\bnew\s+Thread\s*\(|\bThreadPool\.|\bTask\.Run\s*\(|\bParallel\.(For|ForEach|Invoke)\b|\bSystem\.Timers\.Timer\b|\bnew\s+Timer\s*\(`, severity: "warn", why: "Game state must only be touched from the game's own update loop; background threads cause desyncs and crashes. Generated mods use the game's update hooks instead." },
    { pattern: String.raw`\bReflection\b|\bBindingFlags\.NonPublic\b|\bGetMethod\s*\(|\bGetField\s*\(|\bMonoModHooks\b|\bOn_[A-Z]\w*\.|\bIL_[A-Z]\w*\.|\bILHook\b|\bHook\s*\(`, severity: "warn", why: "Patching the game's own code (reflection, detours, IL edits) is powerful but breaks on game updates and conflicts with other mods. Allowed only when the request needs it, and flagged for review." },
    { pattern: String.raw`\bNetMessage\.SendData\s*\(\s*(MessageID\.)?(WorldData|TileSection|TileManipulation|PlayerSpawn|7|10|17)\b`, severity: "warn", why: "Sending world/tile packets by hand is easy to get wrong and can desync or crash every client." },
    { pattern: String.raw`\bWorldGen\.(KillTile|PlaceTile|TileRunner|digTunnel)\b`, severity: "warn", why: "Editing tiles outside world generation changes the player's world permanently; only allowed inside a world-generation pass (files with a GenPass are exempt)." },
  ],
  breakageRisks: [
    { risk: "A content mod is installed on a TShock (vanilla) server, or a TShock plugin on a tModLoader server: it never loads.", guard: "Cyrus picks the flavour per request, says which server it needs in plain words, and the Nxeon installer only accepts TShock plugins for TShock servers." },
    { risk: "Players on a different game version cannot join (TShock servers need the exact Terraria version; tModLoader needs the same monthly build on server and players).", guard: "Plugins target the TShock release new Nxeon servers run (TERRARIA_PINNED_VERSION); content mods target tModLoader stable and record that in cyrus.mod.json." },
    { risk: "Plugin built against an older TShock/TerrariaServerAPI is silently skipped (\"designed for a different Server API version and was ignored\").", guard: "Generated plugins carry [ApiVersion(2, 1)] matching the TerrariaServerAPI that TShock 6 ships, checked by the validator." },
    { risk: "A content mod with missing textures fails to load (tModLoader requires an image for every item, enemy and projectile).", guard: "Generated content points at a matching image from the player's own installed game (\"Terraria/Images/Item_123\") until the creator uploads art, so the mod always loads." },
    { risk: "Multiplayer desync: effects run only on one player's game, or the server and players disagree about enemies.", guard: "Spawning, enemy health and boss summons run only on the server (Main.netMode checks); player effects run only for the local player; enemy AI changes set netUpdate." },
    { risk: "Mod changes the player's world or character permanently, or wipes it.", guard: "World edits only happen inside a world-generation pass (new worlds); save/delete/file APIs are blocked by the validator." },

    { risk: "Endless loops or blocking calls freeze the server.", guard: "No threads, sleeps or unbounded loops: timers count game updates (60 per second) instead. The validator blocks Thread.Sleep and while(true)." },
    { risk: "Mod name uses the Terraria trademark (\"Terraria Frost Mod\"), which tModLoader's terms forbid.", guard: "The validator warns when the mod name contains \"Terraria\"." },
  ],
  outdatedSignals: [

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# devhost — run agent dev work on the BUILD HOST (node-2), not on the primary.
#
# Edit files on the primary as usual (your own git worktree — never /opt/nxeon),
# then run every heavy command through this helper. It mirrors your worktree's
# source to node-2 (/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>, own node_modules there), runs the
# command inside the capped nxeon-build-agents.slice with a THROWAWAY database
# (Postgres on node-2 127.0.0.1:5433), and streams the output back.
#
#   scripts/devhost run [--lock] [--max SEC] -- CMD...   push + run CMD in the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost tsc                                  = run -- npx tsc --noEmit
#   scripts/devhost test [FILES...]                      = run --lock -- npx tsx --test ...
#   scripts/devhost build                                = run --lock -- npx next build
#   scripts/devhost dev [--port P]                       start `next dev` on node-2 (background unit)
#   scripts/devhost bg NAME [--port P] -- CMD...         any background process (worker, preview server)
#   scripts/devhost stop [NAME|all]                      stop this worktree's background units
#   scripts/devhost logs [NAME] [-n N] [-f]              journal of a background unit (default: dev)
#   scripts/devhost tunnel PORT [LOCAL_PORT]             ssh -L so the primary can curl/Playwright it
#   scripts/devhost pull REMOTE_PATH [LOCAL_DEST]        copy results (screenshots, reports) back
#   scripts/devhost push                                 just sync files (run does this itself)
#   scripts/devhost install                              force npm install + prisma generate there
#   scripts/devhost db push|reset|info                   throwaway DB: schema push / recreate / name
#   scripts/devhost env set KEY=VALUE | unset KEY | list extra env for this worktree (never prod secrets)
#   scripts/devhost rm                                   stop units, drop the throwaway DB, delete the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost ls | status | sync                   workspaces / node-2 load / push refs to node-2's mirror
#
# Rules: /root/agent-notes/BUILD-HOST.md. The node-2 copy is a build/run sandbox,
# not a place to edit or commit — your primary-side worktree stays the source of truth.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
# shellcheck source=lib/buildhost-env.sh
source "$HERE/lib/buildhost-env.sh"
REPO="${DEVHOST_REPO:-/opt/nxeon}"

die() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
say() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; }
q() { printf '%q ' "$@"; }

# ---- workspace identity -----------------------------------------------------
worktree_root() {
  local top; top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || die "run this inside your own git worktree of the Nxeon repo"
  top=$(readlink -f "$top")
  case "$top" in
    /opt/nxeon|/opt/nxeon-staging|/tank/nxeon-deploy/*) die "$top is a live/deploy tree. Create your own worktree first:  git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/<name> -b <branch> main" ;;
  esac
  [ -L "$top/.next" ] && die "$top/.next is a symlink (a live tree) — refusing"
  [ -L "$top/node_modules" ] && say "warning: $top/node_modules is a symlink — never 'git add -A' here (see BUILD-HOST.md). devhost does not need local node_modules at all."
  echo "$top"
}
ws_name() {
  local top="$1" n
  n=$(basename "$top" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | tr -c 'a-z0-9-\n' '-' | sed -E 's/-+/-/g; s/^-//; s/-$//' | cut -c1-40)
  [ -n "$n" ] || n=wt
  echo "${DEVHOST_NAME:-$n}"
}
init_ws() {

content.thinking:
There's a reusable pattern here: compiling mods against fixtures, building the jar, and running test flights with RCON checks for plugin status, command responses, memory, and boot time. For my large synthetic suite, I can generate many items, menus, quests, and bosses under raised design limits, compile them, and verify with an actual test flight run, starting with raising the max items cap.

Raising caps changes JSON schema artifacts and the staleness test for build-designer-artifacts, plus affects the service bundle. I'm thinking the cleaner approach is making caps suite-aware: keep the default per-mod limits for single-module mods, but when a mod is a multi-module suite with the CYRUS_MOD_SUITES flag enabled, pull larger limits from SUITE_LIMITS with performance budget warnings, passed through an optional limits field on the validation context so default behavior stays byte-identical when the flag is off. The complication is that the service layer bundles its own copy of the TS validator, so if it still validates against default limits, a 20-item suite would fail there even if the core validator allows it.

I'm now considering whether modules get built and compiled separately or as one unified plugin -- since the AI generates each module's designs with smaller context but the final compile is a single jar, I need to check whether to thread limits through the service's build request only when the flag is on, which means deeper wiring I should be honest about if left undone. content.content:
# Cyrus landing page (v7) A single-page, self-contained static site: `index.html` plus `assets/`. # Cyrus v8: mod structure (declutter, sub-branches, mod suites)
2026-10-11, branch `feature/cyrus-r45-structure`. Flags: `CYRUS_MOD_SUITES` (off). Mockups: `mock-forge.html`, `mock-suite.html`, `mock-declutter.html` (shots in `shots/`).

## 1. Capability manifest (declutter)
One pure function, `usableFor(game, version, ctx?)` in `lib/cyrus/manifest`, derived only from what already exists: the game adapter (routes, asset delivery, asset profile incl. catalog `accepts`, mesh budget, motion capability), the version registry (capabilities such as `itemModelDefinitions`, `dialogApi`, `animatedCreatures`), the designer feature check (`designFeatures`), `GameSupport` (categories, example prompts) and the plan gate (`canAsset`). Nothing is hand-listed per game.

It returns, for the game and version: studios, asset kinds, routes, designers with their component palettes, library kinds, templates, example prompts, part (module) kinds, and `whyNot` help entries.

**Three states, one rule each:**
| State | When | UI |
|---|---|---|
| usable | the game and version can use it, the plan allows it, the host switch is on | shown |
| locked | usable by the game, blocked only by the PLAN | shown with the lock + upgrade (existing behaviour) |
| hidden | the game or version cannot use it (no route, no delivery, catalog `none`, version capability missing with no fallback), or the host switch is off | not shown; game/version reasons become one `whyNot` line in a small "Why is X not here?" help entry; a switched-off feature gets no line (never leak a flag) |

Examples: Minecraft hides the Mesh studio (no mesh route: `meshBudget` absent, catalog `model: none`), shaders/skies/keybinds/HUD widgets (client-mod route `unsupported`), HDRIs, decals, PBR sets. Minecraft 1.21.1 hides item model states (legacy fallback only), 1.21.1-1.21.6 hide Dialog menus. Terraria, Valheim and Zomboid have no adapter yet: code-only, so every asset studio, designer and asset library kind is hidden and only "describe it" + Config + Files remain, with their own example prompts. An unknown game gets an empty manifest (fail closed).

**Applied to:** the studio switch in `StudioShell`, the project page studio list, the library browser and `catalog_search` (kinds the game cannot use are dropped, not shown as locked; per-entry `games[game].fit` stays), the designer palettes (version-only actions/states/layouts), new-mod flow (game, version, category and template pickers), the templates gallery (each template carries `games` + `needs`).

## 2. Sub-branches in the Forge
Selecting a mod pill opens its parts as a second fan beyond the pill (same links, glow and pill anatomy as categories -> mods). Breadcrumb grows one level: Core > Minecraft > Creatures & NPCs > Moth King Saga > Quests: The Moth Pact > Quest designer. Each part node shows its kind icon, a count ("3 items", "48 settings") and a status dot (passed / changed since flight / failed). Click a part: its studio opens scoped to that part (designs filtered to the module; texture/sound studios open on the module's slots). A plain one-module mod shows its part kinds (Items, Textures, Config...) derived from what it contains, so old mods get sub-branches too. Phones: the fan becomes a vertical list under the pill.

## 3. ModSpec v2: modules
`ModSpecV2 = ModSpecV1 + { schemaVersion: 2, modules[] }`. A module:
`{ id, kind, title, summary?, dependsOn[], requirementIds[], assets[] (slot ids), designs[] (design ids), files[] (owned path prefixes, e.g. custom hooks), provides[] ("item:frost_blade", "entity:moth_king", "quest:moth_pact"), uses[] }`.
Kinds: items, creatures, quests, menus, bosses, hud, textures, sounds, models, motions, config, datapack, worldgen, code.

- **One namespace** (`nx_<8>`): every `provides` id lives under the project's reserved namespace; modules never get their own.
- **Migration v1 -> v2:** a v1 spec becomes ONE module `main` (kind from its route/assets, owns every asset slot and design, requirements all). Lossless; `toV1()` drops modules so v1 consumers keep working. v1 stays the engine default while the flag is off.
- **Cross-reference validation** (structured issues, never throws): duplicate ids, dangling `dependsOn` / asset / design / requirement ids, self-dependency, cycles (with the cycle path), an asset or design owned by two modules, unassigned members (warn), `uses` that no module provides (dangling) or that a module provides but the user does not depend on (missing dependency), foreign namespace. With the design files, references inside designs (`nx_ns:<id>` in quests, bosses, menus, HUDs) are extracted and checked the same way.

## 4. Scoped edit and build
- `planScopedChange(spec, scope)`: scope = a module or the whole mod. The plan says what the change MAY touch (its designs, slots, owned files, its config keys `items.<id>.*`, `menus.<id>.*`...) and what is read-only context: the INTERFACES of its dependencies (provides lists with one-line signatures) and the uses its dependents make of it (so the edit cannot break them).
- `guardScopedResult(base, ours, theirs, plan)`: a three-way merge per source file. Inside scope: take theirs, unless ours also changed since base (a concurrent manual edit) -> conflict, ours kept, reported. Outside scope: ours always wins and the attempt is reported. Removing a `provides` id a dependent uses is refused unless the scope is the whole mod. Generated outputs (Java from designs, plugin.yml, config.yml layout) are derived and rebuilt, not merged.
- **Revisions:** still one revision chain per project (one jar). Each revision's engine record gains `scope` and `moduleHashes` (content hash per module). A module's revision history is the list of revisions where its hash changed; no new table.
- **Spend:** build tokens are attributed to the revision's scope; per-module spend = sum over its scoped revisions; whole-mod builds show as "whole mod" (never split by guess).
- **Test Flight:** module flight = the module's export (module + dependency closure) built and flown alone; whole flight = the full jar. Status per module: passed / failed / stale (hash changed since the last passing flight) / none.
- **Export a module:** the closure becomes a new v2 spec with a new namespace; ids are rewritten `nx_old:` -> `nx_new:`.

## 5. Decomposed generation (small AI context)
`planSuiteGeneration(spec)`: modules in dependency order; each step gets only its own requirements + dependency interfaces (not their designs). Per-step estimate from the existing estimator. A whole-mod build is the plan run step by step, then one compile, one jar, one whole flight. Not wired to a model on this branch (no paid calls).

## 6. Caps and performance budgets
Single-module mods keep today's limits byte-for-byte. Suites (flag on) get `SUITE_LIMITS`: up to 32 modules, 48 items, 24 menus, 64 quests, 8 bosses, 8 encounters, 4 HUDs, 16 motions, 200 design files. Runtime caps (live bosses, minions, tasks, particles per activation) are plugin-wide and do NOT grow. `suiteBudget()` warns honestly: periodic abilities per player per second, listeners, config settings, generated classes, expected compile time. The thresholds come from a real Test Flight of a large synthetic suite on 1.21.11 (boot time, RSS, MSPT); numbers not measured are labelled estimates.

## 7. Mod suite vs Mod Pack
| | Mod suite (new) | Mod Pack (exists) |
|---|---|---|
| What | ONE mod built from modules | several separate mods installed together |
| Namespace / jar | one / one | one per mod |
| References | modules reference each other, validated | mods do not know each other |
| Checks | cross-reference + one Test Flight | conflict engine + combined boot |
| UI copy | "Parts of this mod" | "Mods in this pack" |
A module can be exported into its own mod, which can then go into a Mod Pack.

## 8. Risks
- Bigger mods = longer builds and more tokens: per-module estimates first, whole-mod builds show the sum before spending.
- Scope leaks through generated code: only sources of truth are merged; derived files rebuild.
- Interface drift between modules: provides/uses checked on every scoped result.
- Hiding too much: a hidden item always has a `whyNot` line when the reason is the game, never a dead end.
- v2 as the default changes the stored spec version: kept off until the owner decides.

## 9. Owner decisions
1. Name: "Mod suite" + "Parts" (recommended) vs "Big mod" / "Modules".
2. Suite caps (above) and whether suites are plan-gated (recommended: modules ungated, asset gates unchanged).
3. Spend display: per part + "whole mod" bucket (recommended) vs splitting whole-mod builds by size.
4. When v2 becomes the stored default (lazy migration on read, no SQL needed).
5. Hidden items: show the "Why is X not here?" entry (recommended) or nothing.

# Cyrus v8: mod structure (declutter, sub-branches, mod suites)
2026-10-11, branch `feature/cyrus-r45-structure`. Flags: `CYRUS_MOD_SUITES` (off). Mockups: `mock-forge.html`, `mock-suite.html`, `mock-declutter.html` (shots in `shots/`).

## 1. Capability manifest (declutter)
One pure function, `usableFor(game, version, ctx?)` in `lib/cyrus/manifest`, derived only from what already exists: the game adapter (routes, asset delivery, asset profile incl. catalog `accepts`, mesh budget, motion capability), the version registry (capabilities such as `itemModelDefinitions`, `dialogApi`, `animatedCreatures`), the designer feature check (`designFeatures`), `GameSupport` (categories, example prompts) and the plan gate (`canAsset`). Nothing is hand-listed per game.

It returns, for the game and version: studios, asset kinds, routes, designers with their component palettes, library kinds, templates, example prompts, part (module) kinds, and `whyNot` help entries.

**Three states, one rule each:**
| State | When | UI |
|---|---|---|
| usable | the game and version can use it, the plan allows it, the host switch is on | shown |
| locked | usable by the game, blocked only by the PLAN | shown with the lock + upgrade (existing behaviour) |
| hidden | the game or version cannot use it (no route, no delivery, catalog `none`, version capability missing with no fallback), or the host switch is off | not shown; game/version reasons become one `whyNot` line in a small "Why is X not here?" help entry; a switched-off feature gets no line (never leak a flag) |

Examples: Minecraft hides the Mesh studio (no mesh route: `meshBudget` absent, catalog `model: none`), shaders/skies/keybinds/HUD widgets (client-mod route `unsupported`), HDRIs, decals, PBR sets. Minecraft 1.21.1 hides item model states (legacy fallback only), 1.21.1-1.21.6 hide Dialog menus. Terraria, Valheim and Zomboid have no adapter yet: code-only, so every asset studio, designer and asset library kind is hidden and only "describe it" + Config + Files remain, with their own example prompts. An unknown game gets an empty manifest (fail closed).

**Applied to:** the studio switch in `StudioShell`, the project page studio list, the library browser and `catalog_search` (kinds the game cannot use are dropped, not shown as locked; per-entry `games[game].fit` stays), the designer palettes (version-only actions/states/layouts), new-mod flow (game, version, category and template pickers), the templates gallery (each template carries `games` + `needs`).

## 2. Sub-branches in the Forge
Selecting a mod pill opens its parts as a second fan beyond the pill (same links, glow and pill anatomy as categories -> mods). Breadcrumb grows one level: Core > Minecraft > Creatures & NPCs > Moth King Saga > Quests: The Moth Pact > Quest designer. Each part node shows its kind icon, a count ("3 items", "48 settings") and a status dot (passed / changed since flight / failed). Click a part: its studio opens scoped to that part (designs filtered to the module; texture/sound studios open on the module's slots). A plain one-module mod shows its part kinds (Items, Textures, Config...) derived from what it contains, so old mods get sub-branches too. Phones: the fan becomes a vertical list under the pill.

## 3. ModSpec v2: modules
`ModSpecV2 = ModSpecV1 + { schemaVersion: 2, modules[] }`. A module:
`{ id, kind, title, summary?, dependsOn[], requirementIds[], assets[] (slot ids), designs[] (design ids), files[] (owned path prefixes, e.g. custom hooks), provides[] ("item:frost_blade", "entity:moth_king", "quest:moth_pact"), uses[] }`.
Kinds: items, creatures, quests, menus, bosses, hud, textures, sounds, models, motions, config, datapack, worldgen, code.

- **One namespace** (`nx_<8>`): every `provides` id lives under the project's reserved namespace; modules never get their own.
- **Migration v1 -> v2:** a v1 spec becomes ONE module `main` (kind from its route/assets, owns every asset slot and design, requirements all). Lossless; `toV1()` drops modules so v1 consumers keep working. v1 stays the engine default while the flag is off.
- **Cross-reference validation** (structured issues, never throws): duplicate ids, dangling `dependsOn` / asset / design / requirement ids, self-dependency, cycles (with the cycle path), an asset or design owned by two modules, unassigned members (warn), `uses` that no module provides (dangling) or that a module provides but the user does not depend on (missing dependency), foreign namespace. With the design files, references inside designs (`nx_ns:<id>` in quests, bosses, menus, HUDs) are extracted and checked the same way.

## 4. Scoped edit and build
- `planScopedChange(spec, scope)`: scope = a module or the whole mod. The plan says what the change MAY touch (its designs, slots, owned files, its config keys `items.<id>.*`, `menus.<id>.*`...) and what is read-only context: the INTERFACES of its dependencies (provides lists with one-line signatures) and the uses its dependents make of it (so the edit cannot break them).
- `guardScopedResult(base, ours, theirs, plan)`: a three-way merge per source file. Inside scope: take theirs, unless ours also changed since base (a concurrent manual edit) -> conflict, ours kept, reported. Outside scope: ours always wins and the attempt is reported. Removing a `provides` id a dependent uses is refused unless the scope is the whole mod. Generated outputs (Java from designs, plugin.yml, config.yml layout) are derived and rebuilt, not merged.
- **Revisions:** still one revision chain per project (one jar). Each revision's engine record gains `scope` and `moduleHashes` (content hash per module). A module's revision history is the list of revisions where its hash changed; no new table.
- **Spend:** build tokens are attributed to the revision's scope; per-module spend = sum over its scoped revisions; whole-mod builds show as "whole mod" (never split by guess).
- **Test Flight:** module flight = the module's export (module + dependency closure) built and flown alone; whole flight = the full jar. Status per module: passed / failed / stale (hash changed since the last passing flight) / none.
- **Export a module:** the closure becomes a new v2 spec with a new namespace; ids are rewritten `nx_old:` -> `nx_new:`.

## 5. Decomposed generation (small AI context)
`planSuiteGeneration(spec)`: modules in dependency order; each step gets only its own requirements + dependency interfaces (not their designs). Per-step estimate from the existing estimator. A whole-mod build is the plan run step by step, then one compile, one jar, one whole flight. Not wired to a model on this branch (no paid calls).

## 6. Caps and performance budgets
Single-module mods keep today's limits byte-for-byte. Suites (flag on) get `SUITE_LIMITS`: up to 32 modules, 48 items, 24 menus, 64 quests, 8 bosses, 8 encounters, 4 HUDs, 16 motions, 200 design files. Runtime caps (live bosses, minions, tasks, particles per activation) are plugin-wide and do NOT grow. `suiteBudget()` warns honestly: periodic abilities per player per second, listeners, config settings, generated classes, expected compile time. The thresholds come from a real Test Flight of a large synthetic suite on 1.21.11 (boot time, RSS, MSPT); numbers not measured are labelled estimates.

## 7. Mod suite vs Mod Pack
| | Mod suite (new) | Mod Pack (exists) |
|---|---|---|
| What | ONE mod built from modules | several separate mods installed together |
| Namespace / jar | one / one | one per mod |
| References | modules reference each other, validated | mods do not know each other |
| Checks | cross-reference + one Test Flight | conflict engine + combined boot |
| UI copy | "Parts of this mod" | "Mods in this pack" |
A module can be exported into its own mod, which can then go into a Mod Pack.

## 8. Risks
- Bigger mods = longer builds and more tokens: per-module estimates first, whole-mod builds show the sum before spending.
- Scope leaks through generated code: only sources of truth are merged; derived files rebuild.
- Interface drift between modules: provides/uses checked on every scoped result.
- Hiding too much: a hidden item always has a `whyNot` line when the reason is the game, never a dead end.
- v2 as the default changes the stored spec version: kept off until the owner decides.

## 9. Owner decisions
1. Name: "Mod suite" + "Parts" (recommended) vs "Big mod" / "Modules".
2. Suite caps (above) and whether suites are plan-gated (recommended: modules ungated, asset gates unchanged).
3. Spend display: per part + "whole mod" bucket (recommended) vs splitting whole-mod builds by size.
4. When v2 becomes the stored default (lazy migration on read, no SQL needed).
5. Hidden items: show the "Why is X not here?" entry (recommended) or nothing.

content.thinking:
I'm planning to extend studioContext to also select the Minecraft version and compute a manifest via usableFor, then add a small requireStudio helper so each page can pass that manifest into StudioShell's navigation prop.

Instead of editing every page that uses StudioShell, I realize it's simpler to extend the StudioMod type itself with optional game, version, and studios fields, since mod is already passed everywhere -- this way StudioShell can filter nav links and show lock states just by reading mod.studios, and the breadcrumb can pull the game name from mod.game.

I'm defining the set of studio IDs and their availability states, noting that HUD isn't its own studio page even though a HUD designer exists, and that "code" (Describe/Files) should always be usable for any buildable game. For determining which designer studios are available, I'm leaning toward adding an optional `designers` capability list to GameAdapter itself (populated in the minecraft adapter) rather than hardcoding game checks, so availability is derived honestly from adapter capabilities -- though I'm wary of this touching the same minecraft adapter file another change is editing.

Now I'm working out gating rules per studio: texture/sound depend on assetDelivery support in the adapter, model and model-editor depend on mesh formats supported by the profile, mesh depends on a mesh budget being present (falling back to catalog "none" reasons when absent), and motion is gated by profile.motion plus the adapter's designer list but otherwise left open/usable. For items/menus/bosses, I'm mapping each to the corresponding designer kind (item, menu/quest, boss) and checking Minecraft-specific version-based design features, which naturally fall through to not-ok for non-Minecraft games.

For datapacks, I'm checking whether the dataPack artifact availability isn't "unsupported," and for config I'm trying to figure out whether Terraria's code-only setup actually exposes a config studio, since the mock implies JSON settings should show but I need to verify whether the config exporter only supports YAML for Paper-based games.

## Cyrus mod structure: capability manifest, parts, mod suites (r45, branch `feature/cyrus-r45-structure`, NOT deployed, flag `CYRUS_MOD_SUITES` OFF)
Design + mockups: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/v8-structure/` (`STRUCTURE-PLAN.md`, `mock-forge.html`, `mock-suite.html`, `mock-declutter.html`, shots). Report: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/AQ-structure.md`.

**Capability manifest (declutter).** `lib/cyrus/manifest` `usableFor(game, version, { plan?, switches? })` derives, per game and version, the usable studios, asset kinds, routes, designers + action palette, library kinds, part kinds, templates, example prompts and `whyNot` help lines. Sources only: the game adapter (routes, asset delivery, asset profile and its catalog `accepts`, mesh budget, motion, the new `designers` field), the version registry capabilities, `designFeatures`, the config exporters, `GameSupport`, the plan gate. States: usable / locked (plan, shown with the lock) / hidden (game, version or host switch; a switched-off feature gets no help line). Games without an adapter (Terraria, Valheim, Zomboid) are code-only: "Describe it" and Files only. Unknown games get an empty manifest. Applied to: `StudioShell` studio switch (StudioMod gains `game`, `version`, `studios`, `palette`), the designer tabs and the Item Designer action picker, every studio page (`studioContext(id, "<studio>")` 404s a studio the game or version cannot use, e.g. Mesh on Minecraft), the project page studio list, the new-mod flow (templates carry `games` + `needs`; example prompts; "Why are some things not here?"), the library browser and `catalog_search` (kinds the game cannot use are never searched and never listed as locked; `BrowseResult.hidden`). Host switches for pages: `app/dashboard/cyrus/app/_switches.ts`.

**Parts (Forge sub-branches).** `lib/cyrus/structure/parts.ts`: `partsOfBuild(view)` derives a built mod's parts from what it shipped (designs by kind, textures, sound sets, creatures, item models, data packs, settings, code); `partsOfSuite(spec, status)` gives one part per module. `components/cyrus/cosmos/PartFan.tsx`: the selected mod opens into its parts as a second fan beyond its pill (rides the pill every frame); a part opens its studio with `?part=<kind>&module=<id>`, and the studio crumb gains the part (Core > Minecraft > category > mod > part > studio). Switched-off studios are shown dimmed without a link.

**ModSpec v2: modules.** `lib/cyrus/engine-core/modules.ts`. `modules[]` = { id, kind, title, default?, dependsOn, requirementIds, assets (slot ids), designs (design ids), files (owned prefixes), provides (`<kind>:<id>`), uses }. One namespace. `migrateV1ToV2` makes a v1 spec one default module `main` (lossless; `toV1` drops modules). `validateModSpecV2` = v1 rules + `validateModules`: duplicate ids, dangling dependsOn/assets/designs/requirements, self-dependency, cycles (with path), double ownership, duplicate provides, dangling uses, missing dependencies, and references INSIDE designs (`nx_ns:<id>` or a bare id of another design/slot). v1 stays the engine default; `store.addRevision` accepts a v2 spec only with `CYRUS_MOD_SUITES=1`. Engine record gains `scope`, `moduleHashes` (FNV-1a fingerprints, change detection only) and `tokens`.

**Scoped edits.** `planScopedChange(spec, scope)` = what a part may change (its designs, slots, owned files, config prefixes `items.<id>.` etc.) + the read-only interfaces of its dependency closure + what dependents use of it, and the context size. `scopedChangeRequest` is the prompt half; `guardScopedResult(base, ours, theirs, plan)` is the three-way file guard (in scope: theirs unless ours changed too = conflict; outside: ours + violation; removing a provide a dependent uses = break); `guardConfigValues` for settings. `suiteStatus` derives per-part revision, Test Flight (module flights cover the dependency closure; stale after a change) and tokens from the revision chain; whole-mod builds stay in a "whole mod" bucket. `exportModule` = the closure under a new namespace (also what a part-level flight builds). `planSuiteGeneration` = dependency-ordered steps, each with only its own requirements + interfaces. `suiteBudget` = honest size lines (measured vs estimate).

**Suite limits.** `SUITE_KIND_LIMITS` (48 items, 24 menus, 64 quests, 8 bosses, 8 encounters, 4 HUDs, 16 motions, 200 design files) via the new optional `limits` in `validateGameplay` / `validateDesigns` / `compileMod`; absent = today's limits byte for byte. Runtime caps do not grow. The build service (`services/modbuilder/designs.js`) still uses the default limits.

**Project page.** "Parts of this mod (suite)" card (`components/cyrus/app/ModuleTree.tsx`): parts tree with revision / flight / tokens, dependency view, cross-reference checks, "Edit this part" vs "Edit whole mod" (a scoped change request through the existing change-build API; enabled only with `CYRUS_MOD_SUITES=1`), size budget. Plain mods show their derived parts.

**Mod suite vs Mod Pack.** A suite is ONE mod (one namespace, one jar) made of parts that reference each other; a Mod Pack (`lib/cyrus/modpack`) is several separate mods installed together through the conflict engine. The UI says so on the parts card.

**Tests.** `test/cyrus-manifest.test.ts`, `test/cyrus-modules.test.ts`; real run `test/cyrus-suite-real.ts` (synthetic suite `scripts/cyrus/suite-synthetic.ts`); screenshots `scripts/cyrus/structure-fixtures.ts` + `structure-shots.mjs`.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

# AQ - Cyrus mod structure: declutter, parts, mod suites (r45, 2026-10-11)
Branch `feature/cyrus-r45-structure` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r45`), latest r2 (r41, r46, r47) merged. NOT merged into r2, NOT deployed, flag `CYRUS_MOD_SUITES` OFF, no migration.

## Done
1. **Design** (not in git, like v7): `cyrus-designs/v8-structure/STRUCTURE-PLAN.md` (1,370 words) + 3 mockups (Forge parts fan, suite tree + dependency view, Minecraft vs Terraria nav), dark + phone shots looked at and fixed.
2. **Capability manifest** `lib/cyrus/manifest` `usableFor(game, version)`: derived from adapter, registry, designer features, exporters, GameSupport, plan gate. Applied to studio switch, designer tabs + action palette, studio pages (404 when the game cannot use it), project page, new-mod flow + templates, library browser, `catalog_search`. Minecraft hides Mesh, glTF/PBR/HDRI/decal kinds, client-only features (why-not lines); 1.21.1 hides item states; Terraria/Valheim/Zomboid are code-only.
3. **ModSpec v2 modules** `lib/cyrus/engine-core/modules.ts`: migration, cross-references (incl. inside designs), scoped plan, scoped change request, three-way scope guard (files + config values), per-part revisions / Test Flight / tokens from the revision chain, export under a new namespace, decomposed generation plan, size budget. Store takes v2 only with the flag. Designer `SUITE_KIND_LIMITS` (default limits unchanged).
4. **UI**: parts fan in the Forge, part crumb in studios, parts card on the project page (tree, dependency view, checks, edit part vs whole mod, budget, suite vs Mod Pack copy).
5. Docs (DOCUMENTATION.md section), OWNER-ACTIONS "r45", tracker 34.

## Ran
- Unit: `test/cyrus-manifest.test.ts` 13/13, `test/cyrus-modules.test.ts` 18/18. Full Cyrus suite and tsc after the r2 merge: SEE_SUITE.
- **Real Test Flight** (node-2, Paper 1.21.11, no AI, no client): synthetic suites from the verified designer fixtures, 17 design files (8 items, 2 menus, 4 quests, 2 bosses, 1 encounter) and 80 files (44 items, 8 menus, 16 quests, 8 bosses, 4 encounters): ModSpec v2 valid, javac 0 warnings, strict scan 0/0, both flights PASSED (every boss and encounter registered, a boss from the last copy spawned, reload clean). Boot 19.7 s / 18.9 s, peak RSS 945 / 960 MB, MSPT avg 0.4-1.1 ms. Record `structure-r45-flights-2026-10-11.json`.
- Playwright on node-2 (`devhost dev`, fixtures): SEE_SHOTS.

## Not run / not wired
- The scope guard on a real scoped build result (a scoped edit sends a scoped change request through the normal change build; the guard functions are tested, not hooked into build sync).
- Part-level Test Flight and "export part" buttons (functions exist, no UI action); service-side suite limits (`services/modbuilder/designs.js`); AI decomposed generation (plan only; no paid calls).
- ModSpec v2 is not the engine default; HUD parts have no studio (open Files).
